style: cinematic sound-design miniature, rainy city street at 2am, wet tyres hissing, far-off sirens, a lone tenor saxophone noodling from a bar doorway, a young British lad crooning off-key and slurred, sentimental and melancholy, half-singing to himself, his voice then multiplying into a whispered choir of himself, layered, wide stereo, drifting out of sync, sudden hush, one small boy speaking plainly with no melody, collapse to a single low piano note, ending on rain, a cab door and one soft low horn
exclude: drums, beat, bass drop, EDM, trap, autotune, polished pop vocal, anthem, big chorus, female vocal, upbeat
lyrics:
[Intro]
[rain on wet tarmac, tyres hiss past, a lonely sax from a bar]

[Verse]
[drunk British lad, crooning off-key, sentimental, to himself]
There's infinite versions of me. One of them gets home fine.

[Choir]
[his voice splits into many whispering copies of himself, spread left and right, slightly out of time, sax smearing underneath]

[Break]
[everything drops away, one small boy, spoken flatly, no melody]
There's only one.

[Outro]
[choir and sax fold into one low piano note, then rain, a taxi door thuds shut, one gentle low car horn]
[End]
title: infinite yous r1-choir-of-yous-to-one
